# Overview

`CALMeR` (Context-Aware Long-read MAPQ Rescuer) flags reads in long-read
transcriptome BAM files whose MAPQ is anomalously low *given* their
transcript context. It fits a Beta-Inflated (BEINF) regression model on a
sampled subset of reads, computes randomized quantile residuals on the
full table, and writes a filtered BAM plus a TSV of flagged reads.

The motivation: a uniform MAPQ threshold (e.g. `samtools view -q 30`)
disproportionately discards reads from highly multi-isoform genes,
GC-extreme transcripts, and long transcripts — not because the alignments
are low quality but because these transcript-level properties
systematically suppress MAPQ. CALMeR conditions on transcript context to
distinguish noise from biology.

# Pipeline

The standard pipeline is six steps; each function is one stage:

1. `extract_features()` — read the BAM + GTF + transcriptome FASTA, build a
   per-read feature table (MAPQ, alignment length, transcript length,
   isoform count per gene, GC content, percent transcript covered).
2. `clean_features()` — apply standard pre-fit filters (primary alignments
   only, n_isoforms cap, GC range, length range).
3. `fit_beinf()` — fit a BEINF regression on a sampled subset.
4. `score_reads()` — compute randomized quantile residuals for every read
   and flag those whose RQR falls in the lower tail.
5. `filter_bam()` — write a filtered BAM (flagged reads removed) + a TSV
   of flagged reads with their feature values and residuals.
6. `calmer_report()` — render an HTML or PDF diagnostic report.

A typical end-to-end call (requires a BAM, GTF, and transcriptome FASTA;
see `?extract_features` for inputs):

```{r workflow, eval = FALSE}
library(CALMeR)

bam   <- "sample.sorted.bam"
gtf   <- "gencode.v46.gtf"
fasta <- "transcripts.fa"

features <- extract_features(bam, gtf, fasta)
clean    <- clean_features(features)
fit      <- fit_beinf(clean, n = 50000, seed = 42)
scored   <- score_reads(features, fit,
                         filter_method = "mad", threshold = -3)
filt     <- filter_bam(bam, scored,
                        out_bam = "sample_filtered.bam",
                        out_tsv = "sample_flagged.tsv.gz")
calmer_report(fit, scored, out_file = "sample_report.html",
              format = "html", sample_name = "sample")
```

# Adding paralog status as an additional context predictor

When a transcript has paralogs (sequence-similar transcripts on different
genes), reads from that transcript may be ambiguously assigned even at
moderate MAPQ. `make_paralog_table()` computes per-transcript paralog
status from a `minimap2` self-alignment of the transcriptome FASTA.

The example below runs end-to-end on synthetic GTF + PAF inputs, so it
exercises the parser without requiring any external data:

```{r paralog-runnable}
library(CALMeR)

td <- tempfile("calmer_vignette_")
dir.create(td)

# Tiny GTF: tx1 on gene1, tx2 on gene2, tx3 on gene1.
gtf_path <- file.path(td, "ex.gtf")
writeLines(c(
    paste("chr1", "ex", "transcript", 1, 100, ".", "+", ".",
          'gene_id "gene1"; transcript_id "tx1";', sep = "\t"),
    paste("chr1", "ex", "transcript", 1, 200, ".", "+", ".",
          'gene_id "gene2"; transcript_id "tx2";', sep = "\t"),
    paste("chr1", "ex", "transcript", 1, 100, ".", "+", ".",
          'gene_id "gene1"; transcript_id "tx3";', sep = "\t")
), gtf_path)

# Stub FASTA (only checked for existence; not parsed by make_paralog_table).
fa_path <- file.path(td, "ex.fa")
writeLines(c(">tx1", "ACGT", ">tx2", "ACGT", ">tx3", "ACGT"), fa_path)

# Pre-built PAF row: tx1 ~ tx2 at 90% identity, full query coverage.
paf_path <- file.path(td, "ex.paf")
writeLines(paste("tx1", 100, 0, 100, "+", "tx2", 200, 0, 100,
                 90, 100, 60, sep = "\t"),
           paf_path)

paralog <- make_paralog_table(
    fasta    = fa_path,
    gtf      = gtf_path,
    paf_path = paf_path
)
paralog
```

In production you would compute the PAF once per annotation by running
`minimap2` self-alignment of the transcriptome FASTA. `make_paralog_table`
will invoke `minimap2` automatically (declared via `SystemRequirements`)
when no PAF is supplied; otherwise it parses the cached PAF.

The resulting table is then joined into `extract_features()`:

```{r paralog-pipeline, eval = FALSE}
features <- extract_features(bam, gtf, fasta, paralog_table = paralog)
fit <- fit_beinf(
    features,
    predictors = c("n_isoforms", "tx_length", "gc_content",
                   "pct_covered", "max_pct_id")
)
```
